stance_basis: cited as historical source identifying high transit potential corridors, no position expressed
summary: The Niagara Frontier Transportation Study (NFTS) is referenced twice in this window as a historical planning body whose work informed the current transit program. In 1965, the NFTS identified the Buffalo-Amherst and Buffalo-Tonawanda Corridors as having high transit potential, and separately developed an extensive freeway plan (published 1965) of which less than 15 percent was completed due to recognized adverse impacts. The NFTS is cited purely as a prior study source and expresses no direct position on the proposed Metrorail project.
complaint_summary: The NFTS's 1965 freeway plan is noted as largely uncompleted due to public and governmental recognition of adverse impacts of further highway expansion, effectively ruling out major highway development as a viable alternative.
summary_quote: the Buffalo-Amherst and Buffalo-Tonawanda Corridors were identified as having high transit potential in work completed as early as 1965 by the Niagara Frontier Transportation Study (NFTS).
